clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with 1-week fever, progressive headache, weakness and paraesthesias in both legs, and slight neck stiffness. Lumbar puncture showed cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis (140 leucocytes/μL) with mononuclear cell dominance, indicating CNS inflammation. Brain MRI demonstrated hyperintense lesions in the tegmentum pontis and cerebellar vermis on T2-weighted and FLAIR sequences. No direct TBEV-specific antibody or PCR laboratory results, neurological exam details, CSF protein/glucose values, or epidemiological exposure history were documented in the source records.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: CSF pleocytosis with 140 leucocytes/μL and mononuclear dominance on lumbar puncture
Brain MRI showing hyperintense lesions in the tegmentum pontis and cerebellar vermis on T2 and FLAIR images
Clinical presentation of fever, progressive headache, neck stiffness, leg weakness, and paraesthesia

remaining_uncertainties: No direct source documentation of TBEV-specific antibody or PCR confirmation
No neurological examination details documenting leg weakness and paraesthesia
No CSF protein and glucose laboratory results
No documented history of recent tick exposure, outdoor activities, or travel to endemic areas
